title: fix(react): the element data source gate reports a saved view's refused row cap (objectui#10015)
body:
Fixes #10015
Clause-②: no

objectui#10014 made `@object-ui/core` drop a saved view's row cap that the contract refuses (`0`, a negative, a fraction). The drop is correct. On the renderer path, though, it removed the author's only diagnostic: the node's cap went from `0` to absent, and the consuming renderer treats an absent key as "not a mistake". The gate had never reported a VIEW cap, so nothing reported it at all.

This PR makes `ElementDataSourceGate` adopt the pure builder `elementDataSourceRefusedLimitMessage`. The builder is called inside the gate's existing `useMemo`, where it is pure and so safe. The message is emitted from its own effect, keyed on the message string, never from render. A re-render with the same declaration therefore does not repeat it.

## Premise, re-verified on `origin/main` `62597c5`

- **The card's second half is already done.** `ViewDataProvider.resolveElementDataSource` calls the builder and warns (the `refusedLimit` lines right after `composeElementDataSource`). ⇒ this PR is the renderer-path half only.
- **The gate did not call the builder.** `git grep elementDataSourceRefusedLimitMessage -- packages/react` had zero hits at base.
- **No new export is needed.** The builder reaches `@object-ui/react` through an existing export: `@object-ui/core`'s root index re-exports `./data-scope/index.js`, which exports it, and the gate already imports from `@object-ui/core`. ⇒ `Clause-②: no` holds. The two suites that `vi.mock('@object-ui/core')` both spread the real module, so a new named import from it breaks neither.

## When the gate speaks

The view's refusal is reported exactly when it CHANGED what the block receives, meaning a usable view cap would have been written there. Three conditions must all hold:

1. the block's mapping reads a row cap (`mapping.limit` is set);
2. the binding declared no `limit` of its own;
3. the component's own cap is not usable (absent or refused).

In every excluded case the view's cap was never going to land: a binding `limit` wins, a usable component cap wins, and a block with no cap reads none. There the builder's closing clause, "the consuming block uses its own default", would be false. Silence in those cases is the honest answer, not a gap.

## One message per mistake: which wins, and why

objectui#10009's message (a refused component cap displaced by a usable one) needs a usable cap to have been WRITTEN. With the view's cap refused, the only usable cap left is a binding `limit`, and condition 2 excludes exactly that case. ⇒ the two gate messages are **exclusive by construction**:

- **Component refused, view refused, binding `limit`.** objectui#10009's message wins. The binding's cap is what the block receives, and the view's cap was never a candidate.
- **Component refused, view refused, no binding cap.** The gate writes nothing, so objectui#10009's message stays silent under its own pinned control. This message names the VIEW's value, and the renderer's own diagnostic names the COMPONENT's value. That is two declarations with one message each, not one mistake reported twice.

## Measured end to end: real `ListViewBlock`, real gate, real `ListView`

This was a throwaway probe, not committed. It used a stub child grid, counted `console.warn` by source, and recorded `$top` on the wire.

- **BEFORE:** the gate file was swapped to base `62597c5` (blob `38d5e4a4`, zero builder calls), then restored with `git checkout HEAD`. The restore was proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- **AFTER:** `4da41eb5`. The gate blob `2db3dd44` is identical at the final head `3721e254`.

| case | `$top` | renderer | gate, displaced cap (objectui#10009) | gate, view cap: before → after |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| view `0`, component none | 100 | 0 | 0 | **0 → 1** |
| view `-10`, component none | 100 | 0 | 0 | **0 → 1** |
| view `25.5`, component none | 100 | 0 | 0 | **0 → 1** |
| view `0`, component `0` | 100 | 1 | 0 | **0 → 1** |
| view `0`, component `50` | 50 | 0 | 0 | 0 → 0 |
| view `0`, binding `limit: 3` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 → 0 |
| view `0`, component `0`, binding `limit: 3` | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 → 0 |
| CONTROL: view `7`, component `0` | 7 | 0 | 1 | 0 → 0 |
| CONTROL: no view cap, no component cap | 100 | 0 | 0 | 0 → 0 |

`$top`, the renderer count and the objectui#10009 count are identical before and after in every row: **no wire value changes**. The only other warning in either leg was one react-i18next harness warning on the first render; the probe mounts no i18n provider.

## Pins (appended to `ElementDataSourceGate.test.tsx`)

- **A refused view cap gives exactly one message**, equal to the builder's output for view `hot` on `account`:
  - `pagination.pageSize` of `0`, `-10` and `25.5`;
  - a legacy flat view `limit` on a flat-`limit` block.
- **No repeat:** re-rendering the same declaration (a fresh, equal schema object each time) does not re-emit.
- **No double report:** both no-double-report cases above are pinned.
- **SILENCE controls:**
  - no view cap;
  - a usable view cap;
  - a usable component cap;
  - a binding `limit`;
  - a block that reads no row cap.

## Tests (final head `3721e254`)

- **Reproduction on base** (unmodified gate, pins appended). `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/src/element-data-source/__tests__/ElementDataSourceGate.test.tsx` gave **6 failed / 48 passed**. Every red row read `expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`: zero messages today. objectui#10009's control and every silence control were green on base.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/src/element-data-source/`: **54 passed**.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/react/` plus the 23 suites that drive the gate or its row cap (`*elementDataSource*`, `rowLimitNonPositive-9925` ×3, `pageSizeNonPositive-9853/9897`, `ListView.sharedGate`, core `savedViewLimitNonPositive-9928`): **114 files, 1401 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. It ran after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` supplied the dependency dists. `--listFiles` confirms the test file is in the test program.

## Ablation, both legs through `ablation-replace.mjs`

Each leg was run from committed state, and each restore was proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- **Removal.** The adoption line was replaced with `viewCapMessage = null` (anchor 1 → 0, marker 0 → 1, blob `2db3dd44` → `d8c93471`). Result: **6 failed / 48 passed**. The 6 failures are exactly the refused-view-cap pins, and all **11** tests named `CONTROL` or `SILENCE` stay green. This was checked mechanically from the JSON reporter, not by eye.
- **Widening, the opposite mutation.** The builder was emitted unconditionally instead of through the three conditions. Result: **4 failed / 50 passed**. The failures are the binding-`limit` no-double-report pin and the three silence controls that separate this rule from "always report": usable component cap, binding `limit`, and a block with no cap. ⇒ those controls can fail.
- ⚠️ **A test-hygiene fix in this PR's own block.** The first widening run exposed a hole: a red row never reached its own `mockRestore()`, and `vi.spyOn` on a still-spied method returns the SAME spy with its calls. Two silence controls that should have been immune therefore read an earlier row's messages. Fixed in `4da41eb5` with an `afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks)`. Both legs were re-run after that commit and gave the readings above.

## Lint: a proven narrowing, not a repo-wide run

`pnpm lint` is CI's run. Locally, `eslint --format json` over the two changed source files reports **2 files** (the count read from the JSON output), neither reported as ignored, with **0 errors** and **15 warnings**. None of the warnings sits on a line this branch adds (mapped against `git diff -U0 62597c5 HEAD`); the one this branch introduced was removed in `3721e254`.

The narrowing excludes nothing, for three reasons:

- `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting: no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and no `*TypeChecked` config.
- It loads no import plugin.
- No custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem.

⇒ every rule is single-file, and this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.

## Gates, all exit 0 on `3721e254`

- `check:control-bytes`
- `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations)
- `check-changeset-presence`
- `check-changeset-no-major`
- `check-changeset-overwrite`
- `check-changeset-fixed`
- `check:changeset-claims`
- `check:pending-changeset-literals`
- `check:element-data-source-declaration`
- `check:handler-key-reads`
- `check:component-surface-parity`
- `check:test-path-roots`
- `check:vi-mock-override-shape`

**NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-examples`**, which names this file's `useElementDataSourceSchema` example.

- **Reason:** it needs about 35 package dists (its own prerequisite refusal lists them), which exceeds the foreground cap. It is CI's run (`doc-snippet-types.yml`).
- **Why its input is unchanged:** the fenced-example content of the gate file hashes identically at base and head (sha1 `93f9264b`), with one `@example` each, and this branch adds zero fence or `@example` lines.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of fence, reported for filing (reproducible).** `ViewDataProvider.resolveElementDataSource` calls the builder unconditionally, so a binding that declares its own `limit` still gets a sentence saying the block "uses its own default".
  - **Measured with a throwaway probe:** a view `pagination.pageSize: 0` plus binding `limit: 3` sends `limit: 3` to the fetcher and still warns once, with that closing clause.
  - **What this PR does differently:** the gate path avoids this through condition 2.
  - **Why it is not repaired here:** `packages/core/src/data-scope/**` is fenced for this card.
- **Noted, not filed.** In `@object-ui/core`'s `element-data-source.ts` module doc, the paragraph about the view's half of `limit` is inserted inside the composition table, so the `viewType` row renders detached from it. Documentation polish in a fenced file; carrier: whoever next edits that header.

This work was done in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC` (the `domain:ui` seat #1 dispatch of objectui#10015).
